charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
Segment revenue is the sales split management reports to the board: US Refreshment Beverages, US Coffee, International, and (new) JDE Peet's.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: the JDE Peet's acquisition closed 2026-04-01 and reports as its own segment from Q2 2026, roughly doubling consolidated revenue in one quarter -- year-over-year comparisons across that line are acquisition math, not organic growth. Segment totals also run slightly below consolidated Revenue (corporate/eliminations not shown here).

What to watch:

  • JDE Peet's run-rate once a full year of quarters exists
  • US Coffee's shrinking share of the mix as JDE Peet's scales in
  • International growth net of FX (see the FX-impact KPI in the filings)

segmentMargin.title: Segment profit margin
segmentMargin.content:
Segment profit margin is each segment's operating profit divided by its own revenue -- not the consolidated operating margin.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: JDE Peet's opened at a loss in H1 2026 (acquisition/integration costs) before turning positive in Q3 2026 -- the integration-cost curve investors are watching. US Coffee's margin has been the most volatile of the legacy segments as pod volumes soften.

What to watch:

  • JDE Peet's margin converging toward the legacy segments' range
  • US Refreshment Beverages (the highest-margin legacy segment) holding margin as GHOST scales

coffeeVolumeMix.title: Coffee volume, pricing and GHOST
coffeeVolumeMix.content:
Volume/mix growth and net price realization are the two halves of segment revenue growth (volume x price = revenue, roughly); K-Cup pod volume growth is the single-serve category management calls out separately as the segment's core demand signal. GHOST's contribution shows how much of US Refreshment Beverages' volume/mix growth the GHOST energy brand is adding.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: US Coffee pod volumes have been negative every quarter shown, offset (not always fully) by price increases -- the segment is shrinking in units and growing, when it grows, on price. GHOST alone has been adding several points of growth to US Refreshment Beverages, the segment that otherwise would look far more mature.

What to watch:

  • Whether net price realization keeps outrunning negative volume/mix in US Coffee
  • GHOST's contribution decelerating as it scales off a larger base

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
